questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: A train station is ahead.
Signal before you continue.
Slow down and let trains pass.
Stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and let trains pass.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that railroad tracks are ahead. Slow down when you see this sign. Trains cannot stop for cars, so you must wait for them to pass before crossing the tracks.

questions.question: When do you have the right-of-way to turn left?

options.text: A solid green light
A flashing yellow light
A green arrow pointing left
A flashing red light

questions.correctAnswerText: A green arrow pointing left
questions.explanation: A green arrow means you can go in the direction the arrow points. Oncoming traffic must stop for you when you have a green arrow.

questions.question: You may not park:

options.text: On a hill.
In a parking lot.
On a crosswalk or in a bicycle lane.
Within 12 inches of the right side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: On a crosswalk or in a bicycle lane.
questions.explanation: Never park on a crosswalk or in a bicycle lane. When you park on the street, stay within 12 inches of the edge of the road.

questions.question: When changing lanes you should not:

options.text: Check your side and rearview mirrors.
Use your turn signal.
Check for other drivers moving into your lane.
Use your cell phone to call police to check if the road is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your cell phone to call police to check if the road is clear.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check your mirrors for traffic behind you. Use your turn signal to warn other drivers. Look for other drivers who may also be changing into your lane. Never use your cell phone while driving.

questions.question: When riding in a vehicle, small children:

options.text: Can be safely held by a strong adult.
Are safe standing on the floor in the back.
Will not be hurt in an accident because they are small.
Must never stand up while the vehicle is moving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must never stand up while the vehicle is moving.
questions.explanation: Children must be in proper car seats or seat belts. No one can safely hold a child during a crash or sudden stop. Always keep children properly restrained in the vehicle.

questions.question: When you want to turn right, your car should be:

options.text: Near the center of the street.
Close to the left side of the street.
Close to the right side of the street.
Past the center of the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Close to the right side of the street.
questions.explanation: Move to the right side of the road before turning right. Do not cut across other lanes when turning.

questions.question: If you drive in foggy weather:

options.text: Turn on your low beam headlights.
Turn on your hazard lights.
Drive at the speed limit.
Do not drive faster than 10 miles per hour.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use your low beam headlights in fog. High beams reflect off the fog and make it harder to see. Use headlights when you cannot see 500 feet ahead.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: You may use this lane.
No traffic is allowed in this lane.
You have the right-of-way.
You must merge into this lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may use this lane.
questions.explanation: A green arrow pointing down over a lane means you can use that lane.

questions.question: If a crossing guard is directing traffic in a school zone, you must:

options.text: Follow the directions given by the crossing guard.
Do what other cars are doing instead.
Assume the guard should not be there.
Follow normal traffic rules.

questions.correctAnswerText: Follow the directions given by the crossing guard.
questions.explanation: Always follow directions from a crossing guard in a school zone. Slow down and be extra careful around schools and children.

questions.question: Leaving space between your vehicle and others is important because it:

options.text: Blocks distractions from other vehicles.
Gives you time to react to unexpected situations.
Keeps traffic moving at a safe speed.
Keeps other drivers alert.

questions.correctAnswerText: Gives you time to react to unexpected situations.
questions.explanation: Space between vehicles gives you time to react if another driver makes a mistake or an emergency happens.

questions.question: When two drivers reach an open intersection at the same time, who has the right-of-way?

options.text: The driver on the right.
The driver on the left.
Either driver may continue without stopping.
One driver should honk to show they are giving up the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver on the right.
questions.explanation: When you reach an open intersection at the same time as a vehicle to your right, you must yield to that vehicle. You can proceed when it is safe.

questions.question: What color are signs for public recreation areas?

options.text: Orange.
Red.
Green.
Brown.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brown.
questions.explanation: Brown signs show areas with historical, cultural, or recreational value. They help drivers find places when traveling in unfamiliar areas.

questions.question: What do work zone signs tell you?

options.text: It is summer.
You must stop immediately and back up.
Driving conditions are not ideal.
You should drive faster to leave the work zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving conditions are not ideal.
questions.explanation: Work zone signs are orange and mean work is being done on or near the road. Drive carefully when you see these signs.

questions.question: When two vehicles enter an intersection at the same time from different roads, which must yield?

options.text: Either one.
The vehicle on the left.
The vehicle on the right.
Neither.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle on the left.
questions.explanation: At any intersection, if two vehicles arrive at the same time, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: You must turn left or right.
You are approaching a T intersection.
Your road crosses a divided highway.
You are on a bridge over a divided highway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your road crosses a divided highway.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that your road crosses a divided highway. A divided highway has two separate one-way roads with a median or barrier between them.

questions.question: Your tire blows out while driving. What should you do?

options.text: Slam on the brakes.
Hold the steering wheel tight and slow down gradually.
Keep driving normally.
Turn on emergency flashers and keep driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the steering wheel tight and slow down gradually.
questions.explanation: If a tire blows out, grip the steering wheel firmly and stay in your lane. Slow down gradually by releasing the accelerator and avoiding the brakes. Once moving slowly, apply the brakes lightly and move to a safe area.

questions.question: When a school bus stops with its stop arm out, you should:

options.text: Come to a complete stop and wait.
Honk your horn and pass on the left.
Continue when you think all children have exited.
Pass the bus before the door opens.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop and wait.
questions.explanation: You must come to a complete stop when a school bus is stopped with its stop arm extended. Do not proceed until the stop arm is pulled back in.

questions.question: What do regulatory signs do?

options.text: They are placed wherever there is danger.
They tell you what you must or must not do.
They are diamond-shaped and yellow or green.
They warn about school zones.

questions.correctAnswerText: They tell you what you must or must not do.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs are usually rectangular with black text on white. They show rules you must follow, such as speed limits or prohibitions on passing or turning.

questions.question: To pass a slower vehicle on a two-lane road, you must:

options.text: Not cross the center line.
Flash your lights at oncoming traffic.
Use the shoulder.
Use the oncoming traffic lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the oncoming traffic lane.
questions.explanation: On a two-lane road, you must cross into the oncoming lane to pass. Only do this if it is safe and legal.

questions.question: If you reach an intersection where you want to turn but are not in the right lane, you should:

options.text: Quickly cut across traffic to make your turn.
Turn on your blinker and turn from your current lane.
Go to the next intersection and turn there.
Safely change lanes and back up to the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Go to the next intersection and turn there.
questions.explanation: Never make sudden turns. If you are not in the correct lane to turn, drive to the next intersection and make your turn from the proper lane.

questions.question: What is distracted driving?

options.text: Very uncommon.
Extremely dangerous.
Nothing to worry about.
Just as safe as normal driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Extremely dangerous.
questions.explanation: Distracted driving is extremely dangerous. It puts you, your passengers, pedestrians, bicyclists, and other drivers at risk. Staying focused on the road helps prevent crashes.

questions.question: When driving near a motorcycle, you must:

options.text: Give the motorcycle a full lane.
Drive on the shoulder next to the motorcycle.
Let the motorcycle share half a lane with you.
Pass the motorcycle in the same lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give the motorcycle a full lane.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle is a full vehicle with the same road rights as any car. Give the motorcyclist the entire lane width. Even if there seems to be room to share the lane, the motorcycle needs space to move safely.

questions.question: Which statement about emergency vehicles is true?

options.text: They have the right-of-way when using sirens, horns, and flashing lights.
They can use a loudspeaker to give instructions.
They can follow each other in a line.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Give the right-of-way to police cars, fire trucks, ambulances, and other emergency vehicles using a siren or air horn and red or blue flashing lights. Follow instructions from their loudspeakers. Emergency vehicles often follow each other, so only move when the way is clear.

questions.question: When is it illegal to drive below the speed limit?

options.text: When driving slowly blocks the normal flow of traffic.
When in heavy traffic in a construction zone.
Only when driving in rural areas.
When driving in bad weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: When driving slowly blocks the normal flow of traffic.
questions.explanation: It is illegal to drive so slowly that you block traffic flow. You can be ticketed for driving too slowly.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Intersection ahead.
Road curve ahead.
Turn right.
Lane change.

questions.correctAnswerText: Intersection ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that an intersection with another road is coming.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Do not pass.
Do not enter.
No turn on red.
Keep right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep right.
questions.explanation: This sign means a divided highway is starting ahead. The road will split into two separate one-way roads with a median between them. Stay in the right lane.

questions.question: What should you do when an emergency vehicle is approaching with flashing red or blue lights?

options.text: Try to reach your destination before it catches up.
Keep driving but stay out of its way.
Pull over to the side of the road and stop.
Stop in the middle of an intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over to the side of the road and stop.
questions.explanation: Give the right-of-way to all emergency vehicles using a siren, air horn, or flashing lights. Pull over to the right edge of the road when possible. If you are in an intersection, drive through it first before pulling over.

questions.question: If your car breaks down on a highway, you should:

options.text: Stay in your car and wait for help.
Turn on your four-way flashers to warn other drivers.
Honk your horn at passing cars.
Flash your headlights at oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your four-way flashers to warn other drivers.
questions.explanation: If your car breaks down on the highway, signal before carefully leaving the road and turn on your hazard flashers. Park as far off the road as possible where other drivers can see you. Lift your hood to show your car is disabled.

questions.question: If you have a tire blowout, what should you do?

options.text: Take your foot off the gas.
Do not brake right away.
Slow down gradually, then pull off the road.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: If you have a tire blowout, release the gas pedal and do not brake immediately. Gradually slow down, gently apply the brakes, and pull off the side of the road.

questions.question: After stopping for a school bus that is dropping off children, you should:

options.text: Wait until the children wave at you.
Watch for children walking on the side of the road.
Speed up quickly.
Turn on your emergency flashers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch for children walking on the side of the road.
questions.explanation: After stopping for a school bus with the stop arm out and lights flashing, watch for children walking on the side of the road. Always drive carefully near children.
